Hi Sean / Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Orbit Health is interested in moving toward a proof-of-concept but Procurement has a couple of constraints we need to clear before we can sign. Key asks from our side: 

- Purchase Orders must include BU and GL-code fields on the PO line (we attach a template).
- We typically run on net60 for third-party SaaS and require monthly invoices (one invoice per month per legal entity).
- Discounts are applied at PO-level and are only accepted if committed spend is visible on the PO (our system won’t apply tiered % otherwise).

Could you confirm whether Redwood can: 1) surface the PO ID and a line-level BU/GL mapping on invoices, and 2) honor a tiered discount tied to an annual committed spend while accommodating net60 + monthly invoicing?

I attached our PO template (Orb_PO_Template_v2.xlsx). Procurement asked for an official note for our Sourcing team that summarizes any exceptions we’d need to accept.

Hi Alicia — appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front: yes to PO ID and line-level tags, with a couple of procedural notes; conditional yes on discount tied to committed spend but we’ll need to align on invoice cadence and recognition. Details below.

1) PO & invoice fields
- We can populate PO number, line references, BU and GL codes on the invoice PDF metadata and in the line-item CSV export we send to accounting. That will satisfy most ERPs we integrate with.

2) Net60 + monthly invoices
- We support month-by-month invoicing per legal entity. Net60 is atypical for new accounts but acceptable with an approved finance exception. Finance (cc’d: Grace) will confirm the exception path.

3) Discount structure
- Our standard volume discount tiers are applied against invoiced spend, but we can accept a PO-level committed spend anchor. To do that we need: (a) the committed annual amount on the PO, (b) a minimal initial deposit or pre-authorization for the first invoice cycle, or (c) a signed SOW referencing the discount schedule.

Next steps I propose: 
- I’ll loop in Finance to confirm net60 approval and any required late-fee/legal guardrails (Grace, any immediate constraints?).
- Vanessa (cc’d) will send a one-page mutual action plan (MAP) that records commitments, discount tier, and invoicing cadence for legal/procurement signoff.

I’ll also attach a redwood-friendly PO example and a draft MAP for your review.

Thanks — talk soon,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the context. Finance perspective:

- Net60 is acceptable for strategic customers if we have one of the following: a) a purchase order that clearly states annual committed spend and BU/GL mapping, b) a signed SOW that ties to the discount schedule, or c) an initial prepayment covering the first 30 days. 
- For net60 we need to add a clause for overdue balances (standard interest at 1.5% monthly) and require PO routing to billing@redwood.ai for faster processing.
- We will produce invoices with PO number, line-level descriptions, and an exportable CSV with BU/GL columns.

If Orbit can commit to an annual minimum (example: $360k/year), we can grant the 10% tiered discount and accept net60 + monthly invoices. Otherwise the discount will default to our standard list-price or a smaller pilot discount.

Grace O'Connor
VP, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
